pr_title: [ML] fix possible race condition in frequent item sets aggregation
pr_body:
Refactorings done in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94023. improved memory management but also made it possible to run into a race condition in `DelegatingCircuitBreaker`. This change makes DelegatingCircuitBreaker thread-safe.

This change is a quick-fix with low risk. Eventually `DelegatingCircuitBreaker` should be removed. Work on that is underway: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/89437. Under that circumstances the change is reasonable to me. The added locking overhead shouldn't be a problem, re-allocations happen rarely and there is just the `disconnect` case where 2 threads potentially access the structure at the same time.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94023 hasn't been part of a release, therefore I mark this as non-issue, although technically this is a bug.

fixes #95681

This seems to be some kind of concurrency issue.

In a nutshell: A circuitbreaker aware object (transaction store) gets closed, but the circuitbreaker instance itself is already closed. On close the transaction store which uses big arrays internally, frees memory. So the error happens when _reducing_ memory usage, _not_ asking for more. This is how circuit breakers work, every registered memory usage has to be deducted eventually. 

Concurrency, because in `DelegatingCircuitBreakerService` the breaker that fails gets "disconnected", this happens in another thread. So the cleanup thread that deregisters bytes, conflicts with the thread that closes and disconnects the circuit breaker.

I've analyzed gradle enterprise history, the 1st failure happened April, 21st. It did not fail before. In total I found 3 failures in the last 2 weeks.

This might be caused by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94023. This change improved memory management and might have triggered this issue. I guess aggregations now release memory earlier. With other words, it just triggered an _existing_ bug, which we haven't noted before.

I will try to isolate the problem in `DelegatingCircuitBreakerService`.
